meta.methodology: value_score (0-100) = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost_score). fit = editorial fit_score (1-5) x 20. cost_score = 100 - 60 x (entry_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. The published formula reserves 20% for user sentiment, but no sentiment or user-review data is used in any score today, so fit and cost are reweighted 62.5/37.5. Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence).

intro: Your CRM is where conversations and deals live. We keep it separate from the recommended stack, so stack totals do not include it. Many teams start on a shared spreadsheet and add a CRM when it fits.

move_from_spreadsheet_when.signal: A second person works the pipeline
move_from_spreadsheet_when.detail: a cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.

move_from_spreadsheet_when.signal: More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once
move_from_spreadsheet_when.detail: or a follow-up has slipped more than once.

move_from_spreadsheet_when.signal: You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand
move_from_spreadsheet_when.detail: more than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.

move_from_spreadsheet_when.signal: Email and LinkedIn reach the same people
move_from_spreadsheet_when.detail: one record per person stops you double-touching prospects.

move_from_spreadsheet_when.signal: Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month
move_from_spreadsheet_when.detail: stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).

move_from_spreadsheet_when.signal: Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts
move_from_spreadsheet_when.detail: forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

data.pick_tier: Google Sheet first, then HubSpot Free CRM (up to 2 users) when a signal below appears
data.why: HubSpot Sales Hub has the largest small-business reviewer base among the CRMs we checked (60.5% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses) and native integrations with Apollo, Hunter, Smartlead and Waalaxy. Attio suits founders who want a flexible data model.
data.spreadsheet_or_crm: A sheet is usually enough while you are the only person selling, live deals stay under about 20 and most come from your network. Move to a free CRM the week you turn on a sequencer, or once a follow-up slips.
data.also: Zoho CRM Free (3 users), Bigin by Zoho Free (1 user) and Close Solo ($9/mo billed annually, built-in calling) also fit here.
data.note: CRM is a separate category and is not included in stack totals.

data.pick_tier: Free if 2 people work deals; Starter for 3 (3 seats × $20 list)
data.why: HubSpot integrates natively with Instantly, Hunter, Apollo and Waalaxy, so replies and meetings can log themselves. HubSpot currently shows a limited-time lower Starter price for new customers; we use list price. Pipedrive is a strong choice for a simple visual pipeline (75.1% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses).
data.spreadsheet_or_crm: A shared sheet can work for a short while, but at 2–5 a second person usually already works the pipeline, which is the clearest signal to add a CRM.
data.also: Attio and Zoho CRM are free for up to 3 users. Close Essentials ($35/user/mo billed annually) fits phone-heavy teams.
data.note: CRM is a separate category and is not included in stack totals.

data.pick_tier: Starter, 10 seats × $20 (list); Professional when you need forecasting and advanced automation
data.why: 35.5% of HubSpot Sales Hub's G2 reviewers are mid-market companies, which supports staying on it as the team grows. Pipedrive Growth adds email sync, automations and forecasts.
data.spreadsheet_or_crm: At 6–15 GTM people a shared sheet is rarely enough: several people work deals and replies arrive from more than one channel.
data.also: Zoho CRM Standard ($14/user/mo billed annually) is a lower-cost option with native Hunter, lemlist and Smartlead integrations.
data.note: CRM is a separate category and is not included in stack totals.

data.pick_tier: Professional, 25 seats × $90 billed annually, plus $1,500 one-time onboarding
data.why: Professional adds forecasting and advanced automation. Salesforce has the largest mid-market and enterprise reviewer base in the category (45.7% mid-market, 33.7% enterprise of its G2 reviewers). If you pair Salesforce with Instantly, note that Instantly's native Salesforce integration retires on December 10, 2026; Instantly documents OutboundSync or Zapier as replacements.
data.spreadsheet_or_crm: At this size the CRM is the system of record; a spreadsheet works only for side lists.
data.also: Zoho CRM Professional (25 × $23 billed annually, about $575/mo) is the lowest-cost credible option we found at this size.
data.note: CRM is a separate category and is not included in stack totals.

data.pick_tier: Core (replaces Enterprise Edition), 40 seats × $195 billed annually; expect a quote
data.why: Salesforce has the largest enterprise reviewer base among the CRMs we checked (33.7% of its G2 reviewers are enterprise). Plan for a longer rollout. If you send with Instantly, its native Salesforce integration retires on December 10, 2026 (OutboundSync or Zapier are the documented replacements).
data.spreadsheet_or_crm: At 40+ the CRM is the system of record; seat counts and admin rules matter more than the list price.
data.note: CRM is a separate category and is not included in stack totals.
